narrative.overview:
Relay is an Operate product: reviewed company context becomes a bounded representative and campaign, and each customer attempt becomes an attributable conversation, commitment, or proposed improvement. The interface gives the operator one clear place and next action while preserving the records underneath. DM Sans, cool white and lilac-gray surfaces, indigo emphasis, restrained status color, and Lucide icons remain the visual identity; the workflow resets change composition, not the brand world.

The shell presents five working areas—Overview, Company, Agents, Campaigns, and Activity—with Settings separate. Overview derives one evidence-based next action from saved company readiness. Agents is one continuous build-test-publish workspace with a compact picker, wide six-section editor, continuously mounted tester, exact-version checks, and explicit publication. Old destinations remain reachable through aliases, contextual links, search, and record anchors.

Campaigns is one durable record across Intent, Audience, Agent & content, Review, Run, and Results. Partial setup saves preserve incomplete truth. Optional AI brief and content proposals stay separate and attributable until explicitly used or applied to the same campaign. Review checks current authority and eligibility; launch separately freezes the run snapshot. Run owns controlled recipient execution and the mounted browser call. Results is a distinct evidence surface for exact conversations, completion evidence, operator-reviewed planned fields, and honest empty states. Provider acceptance settles operational progress only; it does not prove delivery or business success. Roles, consent, AI identity, participant scope, and human-review boundaries remain explicit. The focused Campaign review returned SHIP for this bounded workflow after final captures and the reported 690/690 plus build/package checkpoint; it is not a whole-product, hosted-channel, or voice-quality claim.
keyCharacteristics: Wide editor with continuous testing context
Visible roles, consent, evidence, and AI identity

rules.name: The State Before Decoration Rule
rules.body: Use indigo, green, rose, and small motion to explain location, action, or record state. Do not introduce color as a quality claim.

rules.name: The Record Readability Rule
rules.body: Keep working copy and controls at 13–14px; reserve 10–12px type for supporting metadata, never for a required decision or action.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Keep containers flat at rest. Use a border, wash, or one small transient shadow to establish hierarchy; never use elevation to imply confidence or model quality.

dos: Do organize destinations under Overview, Company, Agents, Campaigns, Activity, or Settings while preserving a clear owner for each saved artifact.
Do keep inactive navigation groups collapsed and retain old routes through aliases, search, contextual links, and anchors.
Do derive Overview from saved company readiness and current records, then present one next action with its evidence.
Do prioritize active campaign work over optional channel setup and treat only the latest unresolved exact-version failure as attention.
Do keep the agent picker compact, editor spacious, tester continuously mounted, and Save draft / Test agent available from the toolbar.
Do preserve raw editing buffers, focus the first invalid field, and guard route and history exits when the draft is dirty.
Do run checks against an exact saved version, publish explicitly, then pass the active release into a separate Channel draft.
Do keep all six Campaign phases on one durable record with partial saves, exact revision checks, and a fixed launch snapshot.
Do keep AI suggestions and proposals as attributable receipts until an operator explicitly uses or applies them.
Do keep Results separate from Run and distinguish provider acceptance, reviewed evidence, and business outcome.
Do preserve viewer limits, consent controls, explicit AI identity, anonymous/unverified participant labels, and human-review boundaries.
donts: Don't restore the former 18 peer destinations or a three-column agent workbench.
Don't treat historical failed checks as current attention or let optional deployment displace running campaign work.
Don't repeat prompt fields across sections, unmount the tester during section changes, or hide the artifact targeted by Save, Test, Publish, or Channel setup.
Don't bypass the dirty guard for Back, Forward, hash links, search, agent switching, or contextual navigation.
Don't allow viewer accounts to mutate, test, publish, send, or create actions; keep records readable and limitations explicit.
Don't let a draft test, configuration check, release, or prefilled Channel draft imply public activation, live delivery, voice quality, identity verification, or business value.
Don't turn a Campaign phase change, partial save, AI proposal, preflight, or provider receipt into implied approval, launch, delivery, or success.
Don't duplicate execution controls in Results, hide empty planned-field states, or collapse recipient evidence into campaign-level claims.
Don't present either focused review verdict as a whole-product usability, production, hosted-channel, voice-quality, or competitor-superiority claim.
